reasons: Status is correctly characterized: the caps are already mutual on a 12-month fee basis, but the $100,000 floor, the 'charges paid' (not 'paid or payable') basis, the absence of confidentiality/data-protection/gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct/fraud/IP carve-outs, and the one-sided exclusion of liability for loss of Customer data are genuine deviations from the preferred position.

Redline reaches the playbook position with targeted edits: floor raised to $1,000,000 and basis changed to 'paid or payable' symmetrically in both the IBM (p0112) and Customer (p0119) cap clauses, preserving mutuality; changed-character ratios of ~0.10 confirm minimal editing.

Added Excluded Claims paragraph is drafted mutually ('a party's...') and covers confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, plus the preferred carve-out that Customer's payment obligations are not damages — matching the model language without disturbing the mutual consequential-damages waiver in Section 10.

The p0114 carve-back ('except to the extent arising out of IBM's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations') is a proportionate fix to a one-sided data-loss exclusion in a hosting deal; the flagged 0.603 changed-character ratio simply reflects the brevity of the source clause, not an unnecessary rewrite.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, states the preferred position and the fallback, and correctly explains that indemnities and confidentiality/security breaches sit outside the cap.
